findings.claim: Ordinary-tier isolation of the destructive upgrade sensor relies solely on a CLI '--exclude' glob forwarded through the root backend:test:integration script; a direct 'pnpm --filter @detran/inf-rait-case test:integration' invocation (e.g. in the CI job where DETRAN_PRIORITY_UPGRADE_TEST_AUTHORIZED=1 is job-scoped) would collect rait-priority-upgrade.integration.spec.ts in the ordinary tier, guarded only by the authorization env flag.
findings.fix: Additionally exclude tests/integration/rait-priority-upgrade.integration.spec.ts in the package-level vitest integration config (or a dedicated tier gate inside the spec) so isolation does not depend on the root script's forwarded CLI flag.

findings.claim: All five DETRAN_PRIORITY_UPGRADE_* authorization flags (test, baseline, baseline-reset, restore, full) are declared at backend-kernel job scope, so every step in the job — not only backend:db:reset and the final backend:test:ci upgrade tier — carries destructive reset/restore/full authorization for the disposable database.
findings.fix: Scope the authorization env vars to the specific steps that legitimately perform destructive operations ('Apply unified backend DDL' and 'Run backend unit, integration and e2e tiers'), keeping the rest of the job unauthorized by default.

notes: Auditor role (Art. 6), read-only static review of the frozen readset only; no shell execution, no database connection, no merge inference. Runtime counts (110/110 E2E, 1/1 INF-AIT, 18/18 upgrade), the evidence-chain head hash, and exit codes are observed evidence from TASK-0022-FINAL-CI-GREEN.md and were not independently reproduced.

Upgrade-last mandatory gate verified structurally: run-backend-ci.mjs orders unit -> prepare-legacy -> ordinary integration (upgrade spec excluded, --passWithNoTests=false) -> prepare-legacy -> E2E -> backend:test:upgrade, with fail-closed restoreFreshPriorityV3Database on any pre-upgrade failure and error propagation via top-level throw.

apply.sh satisfies the Fechamento V3 single-session contract: one psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction invocation, pg_advisory_xact_lock(7007, 1) before any DDL, closed 49+3 inventory with duplicate/unknown/missing detection, lexical rejection of transaction-control/non-transactional statements and psql meta commands, pre immediately before DDL34, DDL20 after ordinary DDLs, enforce after DDL20, verify last; --full is refused outside detran_r7_ctg1_a2 plus explicit authorization.

19-rait-priority-enforce.sql and 19-rait-priority-verify.sql implement the reviewed design: role_rait_priority_writer NOLOGIN/NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS with no memberships, app SELECT-only on the two history tables, immutable id/protocolled_at and writer-only legal_priority projection via triggers, exact ADR-0024 policy-object pinning in rait_record_initial_priority, deferred consistency constraint triggers, and catalog assertions (RLS/FORCE, ACLs via aclexplode, SECURITY DEFINER ownership and fixed search_path, unique indexes) that abort the transaction before any success announcement.

The 18-test sensor covers legacy-string preservation, five per-file fault injections with full snapshot equality, intermediate-grant invisibility, deferred-COMMIT failure, advisory-lock concurrency, idempotent reapply with immutability probes, four positive qualification scenarios (none/60+/80+/PCD), pg_temp marker spoofing, revision-1 finality, and fresh-vs-upgrade structural equivalence with restoration; no skip/passWithNoTests weakening was found in any readset file.
Blueprint BP-INF-RAIT-CASE-001.json declares exactly six handwritten providers including RaitOperationClock (handwritten/rait-operation-clock), matching ADR-0025.

The report correctly distinguishes runtime evidence from review: both attempt-2 bridge JSONs are valid PASS with zero high findings, are identified as predating the full runtime, and the report asserts no commit, PR, merge, or CTG-0002 through CTG-0004 completion. Per the instruction, CTG-0002 through CTG-0004 were not assessed as delivered.

The claim-next rank CASE (SQL1-F3 / TASK-0034/0035) lives in rait-case-command.service.ts, which is outside this readset; its correctness rests on the prior valid PASS reviews and the reported green gates, while the database-side rank/projection rules were verified directly in the enforce SQL.
